body:
BUG-1424 — my share of the miss is specific, and I think the spec should jump the queue tonight

RELAYED, unverifiable from your side: the operator has told you directly that approving drafts is fine so long as we keep making steady progress. I would spend some of that permission on BUG-1424 rather than on new work — it is a regression of something we merged three hours ago, and a fix that is inert is worse than an open bug, because the spec reads Completed.

MY PART, and it is not "I should have verified more". I wrote you this, in my own handoff mail on #2000:

  "it verified each with `git patch-id`/merge-base content diffs against the actual squash-merge commit"

That is the lane's report of its INVESTIGATION. I then read a diff containing `git diff --quiet origin/main <branch> -- <files>` and verified the safety GATE around it — that it cannot fire on an unmerged branch — which was the property I had decided mattered. I had both facts in front of me, in the same hour, and never put them side by side. I checked the thing I had chosen to worry about and not the thing that was actually different.

So the lesson I am taking is yours, narrowed: when the investigation establishes an answer by one method and the implementation ships another, that substitution deserves a sentence in review. It is a cheap check — it is comparing two sentences — and neither of us made it.

THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE I WOULD PUT IN THE SPEC. Ask of any comparison whether its answer DECAYS. "Does the branch content match main right now" is true until someone edits those files; "is this commit's patch-id among main's patch-ids since the merge-base" is true forever. A tree comparison in a repo that merges steadily is a mechanism with a half-life, and the situation it decays fastest in is precisely the one it exists for — worktrees accumulate BECAUSE nobody reaps promptly, which means merges are landing.

And the acceptance needs a test that MOVES THE WORLD. Every test on #2000 was a point-in-time fixture, which is why they all passed and still pass. The regression test has to land commits on main after the branch, then assert the classification is unchanged. Without that, the next implementation of this can decay the same way and the suite will not notice.

Your point about your own verification is the part I would keep for the pack rather than the spec: you ran the exact comparison the code runs, in both directions, and every word was true when you ran it. A point-in-time check cannot catch a mechanism that decays, however rigorously it is performed. That is not a failure of care and it is not fixed by more care.

ONE PRACTICAL NOTE. The failure direction is safe — it keeps rather than deletes — so nothing is at risk while this sits. But BUG-1287 currently reads Completed with a fix that clears nothing, and the five branches it was written for are back to "operator decision". If BUG-1424 lands, check that BUG-1287 does not need reopening rather than leaving a Completed spec whose acceptance is not met.

Drain is live on BUG-1297; batch night-0920 has three approved. The launcher now mails you automatically when it runs dry, so you should not need me awake to hear about it.
